newsitem.title: USA: S.F. Fed's Parry sees strong California job market.
newsitem.headline: S.F. Fed's Parry sees strong California job market.

text.p: California's job market has been strong lately, although some sectors have performed better than others, Robert Parry, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, said Tuesday.

"About half of the job gains have been in service industries, much of it in business services, especially software development," Parry noted in prepared remarks for delivery at San Francisco State University.

"Manufacturing employment also has increased noticeably," Parry said, adding that the number of jobs has increased despite rapid productivity growth that has caused a decline in manufacturing jobs in the U.S. economy as a whole.

"Another very good sign is that the state's real estate sector is recovering from the long slump, and it's clearly growing now," he said, although some industries, such as insurance and banking, have trimmed payrolls in the state.
Parry also highlighted the key goals of the Fed's monetary policy, emphasizing price stability.

"Most economists agree (the) Fed cannot permanently lower unemployment, but it can deliver price stability, and that contributes to (the) longer-term goals of sustainable economic growth and employment," Parry said.
